utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. For the record, all the accused are here. The Defence teams are also all here. I don't see Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Mr. Lazarevic will come to The Hague today, and he will be in the courtroom as of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for that information. The Prosecution side, it's Mr. McCloskey, yes, Mr. Thayer, and -- Mr. Thayer, please help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin, thank you. Welcome back. I asked Madam Registrar to keep the witness out for the time being so we go through some housekeeping matters. We have been requested -- this is mainly directed to you, Madam Fauveau but it will affect of course everyone else. You have asked us to see if it is at all possible to move the Monday 26th sitting to the afternoon. Of course, that doesn't depend entirely on us. We are working on it; and if there is a possibility to accommodate you, we certainly will, but we will inform you in the course of today. And probably I will receive a reply within the next 30 minutes or hour or so. Okay. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. The other thing is this, Mr. Zivanovic. I just wanted to confirm for the record that we were informed of your request to the Registrar - you never made a request to the Tribunal, to the Trial Chamber itself - to have present, to assist you, your own forensic expert while Mr. Clark will be testifying. We have indicated that we have absolutely no problem with that. It's something that has been done in other trials, including by myself, so you can of course have your expert assist you. However, it would be preferable if, in future, such requests, apart from being directed to the Registrar, that has to be informed of course, are first and foremost directed to the Trial Chamber. This time we are turning a blind eye to that, assuming that there is something new that has cropped up in this case. And so we have no problem with that. And that basically means that if anybody else later on wishes to have the assistance of ex parte forensic experts present in the courtroom while Prosecution forensic experts or Court-appointed forensic experts are testifying, you will be able to do that. However, please do ask beforehand and also keep in mind that some arrangements, seating arrangements will need to be made, especially if there are three of you sitting in the same. All right. There is a motion which came in last week on Friday, and this is a Prosecution fourth motion for leave to amend 65 ter exhibit -- exhibit list. Is there a response, first response from any of you? Basically, we are talking of documents related to PW-105, and three intercepts, two of which are related to testimony of Prosecution Witness 145. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Just to let you know, we would ask for some additional time before we can respond to this motion, simply because most of the people were away from The Hague last week. We have tried to communicate by e-mails and we haven't done that yet. We will need a bit more time before we are in a position to respond. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, how soon do we have to decide, considering that we are talking about documents related to witness PW-105 and PW-145.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Thayer is prepared to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. With respect to PW-145, as everyone is aware, we are in the midst of his cross-examination. I think we have probably about an hour, maybe close to an hour and a half of cross left with him. The issue need not necessarily be resolved before he leaves town. I think we can conclude with his testimony; and then if there is further argument, resolve the issue afterwards. He is here, he is ready to go this morning. I anticipate he will be done before noon today. With respect to PW-105, our schedule, I think, optimistically estimates that he may be testifying as early as first thing Thursday. There is a -- if things move along very quickly, he could go Wednesday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Bourgon, what I suggest is the following: That we try to resolve the issue as it relates to the current witness, to PW-145, the earliest possible. I suggest maybe first -- first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We will do our best to be ready, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure you will. And as regards the documents related to PW-105, we will return to that first thing tomorrow morning. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So there is also another Prosecution motion which was filed last Friday relating to Witness 186. This is a Prosecution motion for leave to amend witness list by adding one intercept operator supervisor as a 92 ter witness and for protective measures. When will Witness 186 be coming over, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he will be available to testify as early as Tuesday, the 27th of February; that's when we have him scheduled. He is available earlier, should that need arise, but that is the tentative schedule for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think we will need again once more here to limit, to restrict the time limit for the filing of the response. You will have up until the end of business on Wednesday, this Wednesday, to respond to this motion. Then there was -- I wish -- I would like to be -- have the Trial Chamber updated on this. There was a motion filed on the 7th of February by the Prosecution seeking protective measures for Witness 157, which is PW- -- would be PW-104, together with an ex parte annex. You will recall that I mentioned this to you last week, and that I had asked you to file your responses not later than last Friday, Friday the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The information that we have, and which we have rechecked, is that none of you filed any responses to this, so I take it we can proceed with disposing of the matter. So the Trial Chamber is seized of a Prosecution motion requesting protective measures for Witness 157 and containing an ex parte annex filed on the 7th of February. We have taken into account the brief -- the brief debate of last week in which we indicated that the Defence teams would be required to file their responses by not later than the end of business day of the 16th of February. Having confirmed that no such responses have been filed, upon agreeing that the arguments brought forward by the Prosecution, in paragraphs 5 and 6 of the motion, justify the granting of the protective measures sought in the same motion; namely, that of pseudonym and face distortion. The motion is hereby being granted. This witness will testify as witness pseudonym PW-104. So that is determined. I do not have any further preliminary matters I would like to address you to. Do you have any? I hear none. So we may safely bring back now Witness PW-145. Mr. Krgovic, I take it that you had finished your cross-examination. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wasn't here for the last -- okay. So you haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I have maybe 15 minutes more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to let you know that Professor Dunjic has been appointed expert for five Defence teams. We asked that he be present during the testimony of all OTP forensic experts. So our motion does not pertain only to him being present when Witness Clark is examined, but also other OTP witnesses Wright, Haglund, Baraybar, and Lawrence. And he will be assisting five Defence teams: Popovic, Beara, Nikolic, Borovcanin, and Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much for that information. This is why I said in future, please table a proper motion to the Trial Chamber because we would be seized with --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I wanted to add. That first we addressed the registry and then the registry told us to send our motion to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And we did not insist on -- on having a proper motion filed, because we knew that this had to be decided before the weekend so that your expert will be here. Although we were all different places, I made sure that everyone was informed and we could decide that in good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Witness, good morning to you, and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, thank you for welcoming me back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We are going to proceed and hopefully conclude with your testimony today. Last week you were being examined by Mr. Krgovic. He will continue with his cross-examination and then we will take it up from there. So, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when we ceased our cross-examination, I was examining you about the contents of three conversations, and we said that those were conversations with UNPROFOR and some other organisations; that was my last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what we were discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to continue where we left it off, with that line of questioning. That's on page 89 of the transcript. "[In English] You can see from this document that he spoke to UNPROFOR members, is that correct?" "Yes. "This concerned relationship with UNPROFOR?" [Interpretation] And your answer was, "Yes." Let me just remind you, those were the conversations that you taped, conversations with the president, or rather conversation with the president, and the other conversation involved Mr. Koljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your question was why I had written that in the first conversation it referred to Karadzic. That's what we were discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what we were discussing prior to that, and what I just read out to you was my last question to you. But if you don't remember, I can refresh your memory again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the last answer I gave you concerned the conversation between Gvero and Koljevic. You gave me that example and you said that Gvero also addressed Koljevic as President. I said to you that in that conversation he identified Koljevic very precisely by addressing him both as President and Professor. I told you then that I was sure that in the first conversation, it was Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in the course of your work prior to this time, and during this time, you did not record a single conversation between General Gvero and any other president or Karadzic, except for the one that I showed you here or the OTP showed you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really remember whether I intercepted any other conversation. As far as I can remember now, after all these years, I did not intercept any conversation where Gvero addressed somebody with that title. I told you that if we were not sure about something, we never wrote that down, and I'm sure that in that case it was Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But in addition to this conversation, you didn't intercept any other Karadzic conversations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have told you, it's very difficult for me now to remember after all these years whether I did or didn't. I simply can't remember whether there were such conversations. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what post Nikola Koljevic held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only guess. I think he was vice-president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could just have a time-frame of some kind for the question, Your Honour, I think that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a very fair comment, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you intercepted this conversation, do you know what post Nikola Koljevic held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have just told you, as far as I can remember, and it's difficult to remember after all these years, he was vice-president. Now, whether he was vice prime minister or vice-president, I really wouldn't be able to tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 6D7, please? Page 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document, Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, and you can see a decision that was published in that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you scroll down, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you know that at that moment, Mr. Koljevic was president of the Committee for Cooperation with the UN and international organisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that now; but as you can see in the text that follows, it says that he was vice-president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, when Gvero addressed Koljevic, he addressed him as President, meaning president of the committee; vice-president, meaning as vice-president of Republika Srpska; and Professor because that was the post he held at the university?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, or rather, I can see that he held this post, too, which I didn't know about earlier. I think there is something wrong with the microphone because I can hear myself talking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can we deal with that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, your microphone is...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could hear my own voice, and I could tell that a mic was on. What you just said is not how it was in that conversation. He didn't say vice-president of this and that or Professor or that. All it said was "President, vice-president, professor."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that's precisely what I did; I enumerated the posts he held. He was the president of the state Committee for Cooperation with the United Nations; He was vice-president of the Republika Srpska; and a professor at the university?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you just said is quite clear to me; but as I told you, this is what was said and written down at the time. The conversation that you showed me last time, I think, was not something that I intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, sir, that when you recorded the intercept, there were at least three people in Republika Srpska who could be addressed as "President" who held the post of president of specific bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that that's what the situation was, but what I told you; but what I told you, that I am sure that it was Karadzic, I can explain if you wish why I am sure. Because I think this sort of leading, He was, wasn't, is a bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, explain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way that we worked at that time was such that nothing was reproduced or put in the transcript that we were not sure of. If we were not 100 per cent sure of something, we would indicate that by some sign, a mark, a question mark, or a brief explanation in parentheses that we were not sure what this was about. Further, the communication itself, this communication of the Main Staff that we were monitoring, our job was much easier when identifying the speakers because of the way they themselves communicated. This is why. They would always have a subordinate answer the phone, then he would connect the speaker with his superior. So some of those people who worked, and I can give you the name of a person that I remember very well, that is Rajko Banduka, who very frequently picked up the calls. He would pass on the calls to his superiors, and probably we didn't hear that. He would call someone at the request of his superior, and then he would ask that person and then he would say such-and-such a person wants to speak to you. We did not tape those parts of the conversation, and we did not transcribe them or reproduce them because at the time we had a lot of problems. There was a shortage of recording tapes, very frequently there was no power supply, electricity was cut. So any kind of saving, meaning saving the energy, sparing the device's motor from working, would mean a lot to us. We always had information like that; and of course because of us, we would never write down any information that was incorrect because that was would take things in a completely different direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you, as an operator, was supposed to record the conversation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, amongst other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then you were supposed to transcribe it on a piece of paper or directly on to the computer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you were supposed to send it to your superior command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It was not your job to analyse or comment about the intercepts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did have some analytical tasks. There were such jobs, because determining what was interesting or not for us, determining if a conversation was interesting or not for us is analysis. All the conversations that we heard, if we had to transcribe all of them, that would be an enormous task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In this specific case when you recorded this conversation, you did not, in the transcript of that conversation, put what you heard, but you added something, too. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what -- what you are thinking of. I can't remember what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You added the name Karadzic, which was not heard in the conversation. You did not hear it in the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained to you just now why we added that, and I think it's quite clear. The way we worked is clear, and what happened before the actual conversations were recorded. I think that I was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not faithfully transcribed what was said on the tape, but you added the name of Karadzic. This is what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name Karadzic was written because probably from this time distance - I really cannot recall every single conversation individually - but the way we worked was that we wrote only what we were sure of, and I am repeating this. This was made much easier for us. Our work was much easier because of the way people on this route communicated, the people in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that means that you did not faithfully transcribe what you heard, but you entered your observations and some conclusions of yours. This is my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying to you now that what was written, we cannot say that it is not faithfully transcribed what I wrote down. It was written down on the basis of information that we had and information that we were sure of. I am sure we performed our tasks properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the possibility of comparing intercepts, for example, between Karadzic and Gvero, so that you could know that they were these persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not do that because we said that in that section Karadzic was not heard, so there was no chance of comparing it with some other conversation, but I had heard him several times before. And, as I said, identification was most often done by people who would be on the line before them. I've mentioned Rajko Banduka, who used to pick up the conversations, the calls before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But in this particular intercept, there isn't that introductory part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not there. It might sound a bit now, but it would take up a lot of our time. There was a lot of work, so we always focused on -- we concentrated on what was most important, what was said, who said it. And in this case the information that was conveyed was definitely accurate, because of the way we worked. And that was how I explained it. You can check in some of the conversations that some parts of the conversation, which might create the impression that these operators, who were subordinated to the Main Staff officers, constantly listened to these conversations. Because sometimes during a conversation, he would directly address, for example, Rajko would directly connect this interlocutor with somebody else. We would note down those parts, indicating that there had been a change of speaker. Sometimes we would not transcribe the initial part where he would be waiting for the connection to go through. It would take ten or 15 minutes before the speaker who was being sought would actually pick up the phone. So that would take up too much tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown now Exhibit 6D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6D14.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to show you the transcript of this conversation now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear - at least that's what we have on the transcript - the last part of your question. Was the last part of your question what you just stated? What was the last part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I will just repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. I think that should be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I am going to show you a transcript of the audio recording of this conversation that was transcribed, and that's essentially what you heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can stipulate perhaps with the Prosecutor that these two things are identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We received this from the Prosecution, so this is the transcript of what was recorded on the audio tape and this is what you heard. Can we agree that this is what you actually heard, and that this is what is reflected in the transcript here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, Your Honour, we've moved on from a different intercept from the one that's taken up the bulk of the conversation thus far. Just so there is no confusion on the record, we are now talking about an intercept that deals with General Nicolai.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the intercept -- actually, of -- it pertains to the two conversations that the witness alleges are with Karadzic. This is one of those conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this transcript, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just looking at it. Perhaps we can scroll down so I can read on, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Chamber and for my colleagues from the Prosecution, this is a document in tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let him go through the text, as he said he would like to do. And when he is ready, then put your question, please. Can we proceed with the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I don't see the end here. Can I see the end of the actual intercept, the end of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That is the transcript. This is all that you heard and recorded. This was transcribed from the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it is being put to you that what you have on the screen in front of you, ending with the words, "Da, da, dobro, probat," et cetera, is indeed the end of the transcript. So I suggest you put your question now, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right. Just one moment. Yes. It's clear to me that this is the end of the conversation. I just wanted to see. Probably there were other transcripts after this one, so the usual codes are not there, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This was taken from the tape that you recorded, sir. Is this what would correspond to your recollection of the content of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember very much when I'm reading it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you like to listen to the tape to refresh your memory, if you wish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to play the audio recording of the intercepted conversation that we are looking at right now. And the transcript will appear on the screen, so that the Chamber and the Prosecution will be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. By all means. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just again, for the sake of clarity, the conversation that we are about to play is located at tab 2 of the witness packet. The conversation concerning President Karadzic, which took up the majority of the morning, is located at tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with that, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about two conversations; one in tab 2 and one in tab 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both of them refer to the alleged conversation with Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the version we are just looking at is the different version which is in tab 2, which is a transcript of recording?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you are listening to now is actually the transcript of the intercepted conversation without assumptions, conclusions, without any additions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Your Honours, but we reversed the order. This is actually the second intercept, and I am going to ask my assistant actually to play the -- the previous conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please compare this audio recording with the transcript that you have in front of you? Are they identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've compared them. They are identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And Karadzic is not mentioned there or any other comments, or there is no one announcing a conversation or anything like that. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this particular recording that we heard, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness 6D15?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is the transcript of the next conversation that you recorded. I am going to play the recording of that conversation as well, so you can compare if the transcript is identical to the audio recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to compare the transcript, before you, with what you heard on the recording, and could you establish that they were identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you wanted to be sure that a certain person participated in a conversation, did you use a document or some other source to confirm who the interlocutors were? In this particular case, you claim it was Karadzic. Did you do this, did you conduct any analysis to establish that it was indeed Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could hear the other person on the line, and in this case we were not able to hear, then we would make a comparison, or rather, we would go and listen to one of the conversations that we had, that we had recorded. And this is how we would establish who the participants were, if we were not sure about the identity. In this particular case, we were unable to do that because, as you could hear yourself, you can't hear the other voice on the line. You could just hear some minor background noise, but no identifiable voice. And in cases where we were not sure, we would also contact the army. We would assist each other if we were not sure. We would have them listen to a conversation if we wanted to be sure about a word or a facility or a person, and that's what our method was. We -- we wanted to make absolutely sure about the identity and about what was recorded, that it was accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So let us conclude, sir. In this case, you couldn't hear the other person on the line. You didn't hear the name Karadzic uttered, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular conversation one cannot hear that. I can repeat to you what I said earlier. I don't remember exactly what preceded this conversation. But the way, the method of our work, the method of recording was such that we only wrote down things we were sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please just answer my question, please. You didn't hear the name Karadzic you uttered and you didn't hear the other participant in the conversation; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct and I confirmed that. In this conversation, we didn't that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't have the other in order voice, to make the comparison, and you didn't have any additional documents in order to make analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you answer this question, Mr. Thayer, I noticed you standing up and then sitting down again. Do you wish to --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just second-thought my objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Witness, I suppose you can answer the question. It's being suggested to you by Mr. Krgovic to agree that you didn't have the other voice to make the comparison, and you didn't have any additional documents in order to make an -- a proper analysis. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wouldn't fully agree because, as I have said earlier, after this time lapse, it's very difficult to know what work we did before the conversation ensued or followed. And as I said to you, we did have certain samples of conversations that we would use, so that if, for example, a new voice appeared, we would set it aside so that we could give it to our colleagues coming in the next shift so that they could use it for comparison. I can't remember now 100 per cent. I can't be certain and tell you: Yes, we absolutely did or we absolutely didn't. Our method of work was such that we made no assumptions. We didn't write down anything that was based on assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit P02375A and B, which is 1074 on 65 ter list. I'll give you the ERN number: 03 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0320-1098, 0320-1099. Could you please scroll down? The next page. Conversation 536. The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you can see here at the bottom, you noted down, "Today at the Supreme Command headquarters, only General Gvero is present."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: There is no intercept here, just your statement about Gvero being there on that day at the Supreme Command headquarters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was our conclusion, which was based on a conversation most likely; a conversation between the subordinates. Very frequently, they would say themselves this and that person is present, this and that person is absent. This is what the subordinates would say, and we believed that only the information gleaned from the conversation was important, and not the entire conversation. So this is how we saved time. . That was something that we wrote down, this particular fact, which was probably taken from the conversations on that day. That fact was important on that day because that was the day of the events in Srebrenica, and it was important that General Gvero was the one who was at the Main Staff, main headquarters. When I say that he was the only one there, that did not include the support staff; no, it only pertained to senior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the Supreme Command is and where Supreme Command headquarters was located of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I think that the headquarters was located in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say here "Main Staff;" it says the "Supreme Command?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm no military expert to draw a distinction between the supreme staff and -- Supreme Command and Main Staff. All I know is that Mladic was Chief of Staff, and Karadzic was the Supreme Commander or something like that. This is what I wrote down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I am suggesting to you that the Supreme Command was located at Pale, and that Gvero was not a member of the Supreme Command and did not sit at the Supreme Command headquarters at the time you noted this down. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you. I just noticed now that we wrote here "Supreme Command" for some reason. It's possible this was an omission on our part, but I am telling you, again, that I am no military expert to be able to draw a distinction between the Supreme Command and the Main Staff. In my mind, there is no great difference. I don't know what each term stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you see no difference between the Supreme Command and Main Staff. You see no difference between the president of one body and president of another body. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that's not what I said, that I see no difference between president of one body and president of another body. I know very well who presided over what and who was what. But when it comes to the Supreme Command, well, I'm trying to find in the text above, Main Staff, Supreme Command. Why we wrote down Supreme Command here, I have no idea. This was probably a mistake on our part. And you know in haste one makes mistakes. I know that he was with the Main Staff. I know that. Why we wrote this down, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Which means that when entering your comments, you made mistakes. Is that the conclusion that we should draw, based on what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you something: It is possible that there were mistakes. I am sure that you will find mistakes in dates. You know, in haste it's normal to make mistakes. Under the circumstances we worked, we wanted to forward as much information as possible, and I'm sure that there were typos and mistakes in expressions we used. Mistakes are possible in all kinds of work. And it is possible that we did make mistakes, but those were not detrimental mistakes. Now, whether we said the Main Staff or the Supreme Command headquarters, well, in my mind there is no great difference there. But once again, I'm no expert when it comes to military terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Based on that, it would seem that Gvero was at the Supreme Command. Is that what you are claiming, or are you now saying that what is written down here is not accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think at this point we've exhausted the questions on this topic. I think he's answered the question a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so, too. I think that you need to move on, Mr. Krgovic. And, Witness, you also need to keep your answers short as possible, because many a time you are really going, beating around the bush, basically, at the end of the day. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown 6D44.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document sent by Gvero, or sent to Gvero several days later where. Contrary to what you say, Gvero is questioned here as to why he had contacted the UN and the representatives of the international community without consulting the president prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll down so that the witness could read the whole document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please read the last paragraph especially attentively. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could you please turn off your microphone. I've read it. Now your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't hear the conversation, or rather, you didn't hear the other participant in the conversation. You didn't hear the name of Karadzic uttered. You didn't do a comparative analysis. And I am telling you, I'm putting to you on the 11th of July, Karadzic was the last person with whom Gvero would talk to, because they had had a conflict since April of that year and ceased any communication at that point. There was only written communication where Karadzic questioned Gvero as to why he had not informed him of his activities. I am putting to you that in that conversation, you wrongly identified the other person as Karadzic. Now, looking at all of these documents, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me read this all the way to the end and examine this claim of yours that he criticises Gvero for not informing him previously. Could you enlarge the document, please? Could you zoom in, please? Yes, and then scroll down. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I can give you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No need for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I can tell you: As I understood you, you said that in this order he wants Gvero, or rather, he criticises him for not informing him. And as I can see he is not criticising him for not informing him, but he is criticising him for making contacts independently of the Ministry of Information, and he should normally contact them through this ministry. I don't see it saying anywhere that he criticises Gvero for not -- for not consulting him earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you read this sentence that you -- that -- where it says that Gvero contacted without authorisation international organisation. He did it without prior approval?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Does this order have a different tone from that conversation that you intercepted? You know the spirit of that conversation, and you can now read the document. Would you agree that the nature of those two sources is completely opposite?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is dated the 17th of July, which is to say after the events. I wouldn't be able to say now. I wasn't involved in all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And had you been updated with all these documents that I showed you, would then your assumption that it was Karadzic have changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot go into the relationship and, as you say now, they were -- they had such-and-such a relationship or their relationship was like this. I -- probably now I really wouldn't be guided by this about what things were actually like, but our work made it possible for us to be certain in our decisions, and, again, I repeat we were definitely writing only what we were sure of. I don't want to keep repeating myself anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you wrote what you were sure of, not what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. He's answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's answered and reanswered it and reanswered it. I think what needs to be made clear is this, and once and for all and we can close the chapter on this here. You agreed beforehand that the name of -- name Karadzic was never actually mentioned during both of these intercepts, and it was your conclusion that still one of the interlocutors was Karadzic. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These transcripts, in this part of the conversation, this was not mentioned, but I don't want to repeat again what I said before. So I agree with you as far as these transcripts are concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And one final question on my part on this. In both these intercepts, although the name Karadzic is not specifically mentioned, in both of them there is use of the word "President." Did that carry any weight in your judgement when you came to conclude that the other interlocutor was Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it did have weight, but I say it again: We were sure of that because - probably, I cannot be 100 per cent sure - before that there was a conversation between their subordinates, the people who actually connected the lines. I don't recall any of the high-ranking officers on that route that we were monitoring, dialing any call himself. This was always done for him by his subordinate, who would then connect him to the collocutor. I don't want to repeat myself again. I explained the way in which they worked and which helped us in our work a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This last part of your answer, when you said that probably there was a conversation that preceded the one we are talking about, it's an assumption of yours because you didn't record it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this time period, I mean I don't recall everything. We would need to have the actual conversation and then go back. I mean we never really did anything like this for this particular purpose. What we were doing was trying to compile as much information as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you the Friday before last that if a conversation was not heard or recorded from the beginning and was not transcribed right away, you would indicate that at the top. Do you recall that that was the practice; if you don't hear the conversation or if you don't record it from the very beginning, you would indicate that with a particular mark. Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in these two specific intercepts, there is no such indication that the conversation was not recorded or heard right from the beginning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This conversation between these two collocutors was recorded from the beginning. It was recorded from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On my list, we need to update it. Who is going -- who is going next? Mr. Zivanovic, are you cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You had indicated about 30 minutes. Do you stick to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 20 minutes, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a break at half past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, we have information that other than yourself, a military unit worked at the same facility and that premises where you worked and the premises where this military unit was were separated by a kind of panel, so that it was actually -- you were not in the same room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He said "no," but it was translated as "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't confirm either way. What was your answer to Mr. Zivanovic's question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the transcript is accordingly corrected. Thank you for your cooperation, both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To clarify this, does that mean that the rooms where you worked, it was possible to enter directly into the rooms of this military unit that was at the same facility? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I just refer to the part of the transcript that starts on line 17 of the previous page, and ending with my intervention, line 22. Unfortunately, the most important part of the whole conversation; namely, the witness's reiteration that he had answered in the negative to your question before, again, does not show up. So for the record, the witness had answered "No" to your question. Thank you. And I thank Judge Prost for drawing my attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that amongst other things, one of your tasks was to record these conversations into the computer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I see from your statement that you entered the dates manually when you did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I also see from your statement that each conversation had its serial number, so I am asking you now if this serial number was assigned automatically by the computer, it was programmed to add it automatically, or the serial number was entered manually, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We entered the ordinal number, actually, not the serial number, manually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also explained that sometimes you would put into your reports what you received from the listeners belonging to the Bosnian Muslim army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what form were these reports received in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean whether it was text or whether it was a kind of recording or other kind of entry?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. How did you receive these reports in order to be able to enter them into the computer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that, we received the text on diskettes, the old-fashioned diskettes used by 286 computers. I don't know how many inches they are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were they encoded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we received them, they were not protected; when we received them from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if you received the texts before they were sent off, or did you receive them after they had already been sent off to their command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really couldn't say. If something was very urgent to them, they would probably send it off first and then give it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, you received texts on diskettes that were not coded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you identified a number of conversations where there was a mistake in the date. You recall that in your statement to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you a specific transcribed conversation that you had. It is on the Prosecutor's list, 1190.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please specify if it is 1190A or C, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. [Interpretation] I have 1190. I don't have anything else on this list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem, Madam Registrar? I think Mr. Zivanovic, if he is going to show it to the witness, we need the Bosnian or Serbo-Croat one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the B/C/S version is 1190C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have it, Madam Registrar? It's not in the system, so I think we need to find a hard copy of it and put it on the ELMO. Yes, Madam Usher, could you kindly assist? And it's only the top. Yes, yes. The part on the top, at the top. Yes, stop there, and this. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 1190C is a typo; that should be 1190B. That is in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you ready with your question? Can we proceed, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this conversation that you see on the monitor here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the first one or the one underneath?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall it just by looking at it like this. I cannot recall it by the content either. There is no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the bottom of the document to see if it's your mark there at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I just want to make sure that this is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is not being broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, if you can please tell me, since this is not a conversation that is transcribed word for word, so it is not the whole text of the conversation, this is just a summary of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one at the top? Can you please scroll up again, so I can see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am only asking you about the first intercept; the others are not the topic of this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And it is written, "We have learned the following information from the conversation."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And, now, can you tell me here in parentheses, there are the following words, "Command in Vlasenica." Are those words actually words spoken by the interlocutors, or is that your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The words spoken by the interlocutors because at the top it says, "We learned the following information from the conversation." One of those pieces of information is mentioned, so this is the information we learned from the conversation. We noted down the information that we learned from the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me why you put this in parentheses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could separate it with commas, you could use parentheses, you could use slashes. It's just for the sentence to make sense. There is no particular reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that one of the speakers said that the secret name "Zlatar" indicates the command in Vlasenica and that you heard that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I cannot remember word for word what was said; but for sake of clarification, all of these routes, it's not the way you think and assume that we just worked off the top of our heads. We had diaries where we recorded the routes, we would survey electronically those routes, and we would write down all the information that was of interest in relation to a specific route. If we said that Zlatar was the command in Vlasenica in the diary, then we acquired this information that the security chief at Zlatar was Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic; that would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have to take this up again after the break. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me remind you, you answered my question by saying that you certainly didn't write this down without any basis, but rather that in various notes and diaries you had various names. I just wish to ask you this: Whether this statement of yours about the command being in Vlasenica, was it something that came from your previous notes or from the content on the conversation between these two persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely, this was previous knowledge that we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, one can rephrase the question in a different manner. Was this the first time, as far as you are concerned, that you heard of the name "Zlatar," or had you heard of the word "Zlatar" before, and were you aware of its connotation, its meaning, since it was obviously a code-name? Were you aware of the code-name significance of that word, "Zlatar," before this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I knew that. I can see that based on the date. And we also had such information, as I've told you, in our diaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's clear enough, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, if that is the case, did your immediate command know what the term "Zlatar" stood for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They definitely did know. Because all information we received, we thought it wouldn't hurt if we put additional information in parentheses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you do this in other conversations as well, or was it done on in this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the words in parentheses, only that. What it says in parentheses, "Command in Vlasenica."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've told you earlier, we put information in parentheses that was supposed to clarify something in a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you thought it was necessary to note down for your superiors that the term "Zlatar" stood for the Command in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that was routinely written down. I don't know whether I thought it was necessary. I simply had that information, and I put it in parentheses. I can't remember that it was precisely for this reason or for that reason. We generally had that information for some time before this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this term, "Command in Vlasenica," was there just one command headquarters, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now exactly. If we wrote this down, then there was command headquarters there, because we wrote down the information that was in our possession, and I can't remember that now. But since I wrote this down then, yes, there was such a headquarters there and we knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, but it seems that you didn't quite understand my question. I didn't ask you whether there was command headquarters in Vlasenica; I asked you whether there was just one in Vlasenica. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were several headquarters in Vlasenica. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you look at the second paragraph, please. It says there, "Secret code for Rudo is Cetinar" Was it something that was uttered by the speakers in this conversation, or was it something you arrived at by way of inference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely, it says here as a new piece of information. This is how it's presented, that the secret code-name for Rudo is Cetinar, and then the rest of the sentence. I'm sure this is what we learned in this conversation. We learned about the secret code.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are trying to say that one of the speakers said to the other speaker or utter these words, that the secret name for Rudo is Cetinar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, such things would happen. It's not like they never happened. I am sure that it came from the speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, here in the continuation, it says, that through Palma, and in parentheses, it says, "Zvornik." Was this again uttered in the conversation that Palma stands for Zvornik, or is this something you knew prior to this and then you put this in this notation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is based on our old information. What we learned in this conversation that was new is that they inquired about Popovic; and as for Palma, we knew about that earlier than this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you that knew about Palma, are you trying to say that the secret code-name for Zvornik was Palma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the secret code-name for the route, for radio relay route, yes. The secret name for this radio relay route was this. This was the route used by Zvornik. I'm sorry. I got it all muddled up a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the town of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the town, but the location, the location where the command headquarters in Zvornik was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Defence team for Mr. Beara. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, I would like to put several questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the OTP, you wrote down that you found employment when one of your friends, whose name I'm not going to mention, interceded on your behalf. I would like it know whether before you started working, you went to some sort of training, any kind of training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just a second to let me clarify. Are you referring to these particular assignments and duties?

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Any type of training regardless of whether it was for this type of work or some other type of work, any kind of training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "any kind of training?" Do you see as training the fact that I completed secondary school for electrical engineering, or do you think that being a member of ham operators' club since 1978 represents training as well? Are you referring to these particular types of duties that I had at the northern location?

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Precisely that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no training prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness 1380? A is the English version, and B is the Serbian version, so could we have it on the split screen, please. This is the 65 ter number that I gave you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: When answering questions put by my colleagues, you said that you drew conclusions on the basis of analyses. My first question pertaining to that is this: Did other operators employed in those locations also conduct these types of analyses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've told you, the main analysis, which was the first one to be done, is to decide what was important and what wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: If you look at the conversation, which is shown on the screen now, tell me, please, is there a tape with this conversation? Did anybody from the OTP, when proofing you for this testimony, give you a tape or play you a tape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to look at this first. Could you please scroll down so that I can see the rest of it? Yes, yes. I didn't listen to the conversation, but I read this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Since you've read it, read the conversation, my question will have to do with the mark entered at the right side at the top. In the English version, it says only "state secret;" but in the Serbian version, in addition to "state secret," it also says "very urgent."

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: You basically recorded this conversation, at least judging by the code given here. Now I'd like to know whether, after analysing this conversation, you concluded that this was something that could be termed a state secret and was very urgent, or whether you drew this conclusion on the basis of some other parameters; and if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every document we sent was a state secret, and this is what should be -- should have been placed on every document. As for "very urgent," we used that to denote the urgent nature of a document. And since this document has a certain content, has a certain urgency, we sent it with this mark, but it's true that it was us who conducted the analysis of urgency of a certain document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: I went over all intercepts in this notebook, and it doesn't say "state secret" on any other conversation except for this one. So none are denoted as "state secret" except for this one, and then there are some other conversations which have "very urgent," which are marked as very urgent. So I wouldn't agree with you that every document said "state secret." But now that you have read this conversation, I'd like to ask you, on the basis of what did you establish that speakers in this conversation, Ljubisa Beara and Stevo from the army Republika Srpska, as you say, Main Staff, on the other side. Would you please read this conversation and tell me on the basis of what did you identify them as such.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you have the identification of Stevo himself, who addresses Ljubo by his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you there, Stevo identifies Ljubo by his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me where it says "Beara" then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said earlier, that the conversations that preceded intercepts, when they were making the connection, I explained that process earlier to you. And I explained why we were sure that it's precisely these particular speakers. Normally, at the beginning of a conversation when the link was made, when they were connected, their subordinates would give certain identifications and then they would connect the senior officers, and then the intercept that follows would begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to try to prove to you that that wasn't on the basis of that, in this particular document, that you did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could we please see page 2 of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know. I'm sorry to object. At line 41, 1, we've stopped getting LiveNote, and Ms. Condon as well. Nobody has LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We do. So we need to address that. Thank you for pointing that out to us, Mr. Meek, because we wouldn't have been able to be aware of it. So I think we need to stop here for the time being. Mr. Zivanovic, do you -- do you have the LiveNote transcript or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do in the centre, but my individual terminal is gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. All right. Do you think we could follow -- do you think we can follow -- we can proceed by following the transcript mode on the main monitor or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's possible, but right now we have two documents on the centre screen. So that causes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Meek. We will address the problem straight away. In the meantime, Madam Fauveau, the Registrar has communicated to us that it is possible to transfer the 26th February sitting from the morning to the afternoon, as per our recommendation to them. So please take note of it, all of you. On that day, we will be sitting in the afternoon rather than the morning. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the meantime, while we are waiting for this to be adjusted, Mr. Bourgon and the others, I had asked you, if possible, to come back with your position on the Prosecution -- last Friday's Prosecution motion to amend the 65 ter exhibit list, only insofar as it relates to this witness. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We are of the view that we would like to respond to both for Witness 145 as well as for Witness 105 together, because they were put in the same motion. And we are ready to do so, but there is an argument I would like to make in this respect, Mr. President, after this witness testifies. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, is it scrolling now or -- Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have LiveNote now, and it started at -- well, with Ms. Fauveau saying, "Thank you" at page 1. So, apparently, the LiveNote is working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And Ms. Condon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can follow with the monitor in the centre. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I thank you so much for your cooperation. So Mr. Mrkic, I think you can continue with your questions, with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 2 of both versions of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, you only need to bother about the first half of that page in the B/C/S version, so we don't need to read the bottom part or the second half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the part beginning with the word, "They are taking." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read that section aloud so that we can clarify that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To read that aloud, "They're taking their names but that doesn't matter. We can, you know how, request that the ICRC ..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you there? Can you please clarify what "ICRC" is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
utterances.text: International Committee of the Red Cross. "... escort them to us and they can be exchanged here as written in the contract. We had no plans to kill them, the mother-fuckers, but to exchange them."

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can now look at document 1381 on the 65 ter list. The English version is A, and the Serbian version is B. It's a short conversation. The Serbian version does not correspond to the -- yes. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: My question practically is the same as the one for the previous conversation. Can you try or can you at least say that you -- can you say that you can come to the same conclusion as in the previous case on the basis of reading the conversation, that you -- that was how you identified the speakers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question as phrased contains an assumption that is not made explicit in the question. I just ask that it be rephrased because it's referring to something that's not specified at all. He says, "Same conclusion as in the previous case on the basis of reading the conversation." If we could just have some more clarity the on the question, I think that would be more helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can rephrase it myself. Sticking to this particular intercept, Witness. On what basis did you come to the conclusion that again once more this was a conversation between Beara and Stevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on -- we wrote down here that we registered, again, or recorded a conversation between Beara and Stevo. Based on the previous communication, since it's been written here again, it means another conversation by the same speakers. It's the same channel. So, again, I don't want to repeat myself too much. But if I can be specific, if we're talking about the previous conversation and then the following conversation, it's very easy to identify the speakers by their voice modulation; that can also be another reason. Right now I can't recall whether this conversation was preceded again by them being connected by their subordinates, who were listening to the conversation and then who were connecting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MRKIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly now, you are leaving open the possibility that while analysing the previous conversation and comparing the frequencies and the channel of that conversation and the topic of that conversation, you came to the conclusion that it was Ljubisa Beara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-145 [Resumed]
